steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Hmm... the usual stench of the sewers, and spots where the light doesn't reach.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: These alleys are all the same.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Urban planners probably can't afford to invent new ways to do their jobs at the speed these cities pop up out of the barrenlands.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: It's just too bad that you miss out on the local scenery if you use these nooks and crannies too much.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Am I right, my good subordinate? Isn't it better to get a view of the city from above?
A gust of wind blows through the empty alley.
All the un-exhaled smoke rings swirl back into the cracks in his metal. The Tin Man wonders if this is an opportune time to hack a few coughs as if choking.
A lighter floats right in front of him as soon as the embers of his cigarette die out.
'Banal' is such a lamentable assessment for a city like this with no history.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: ...Ho'olheyak.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: You were supposed to make contact three days ago.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Oh? I had the impression that you're not particularly punctual yourself.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: If you could just tone down your volume. Why did you pick this place for our meeting?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Did you forget? The factory in District 13 is close by.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Did you find the item from the other day?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Yes, but unfortunately there are only fragments left. Fragments of... stars, with no way to guide the lost.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: And Kristen? Where is she?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Are you watching the sky?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: You get a clearer view of the sky without the skyscrapers around.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Do you think Kristen might be hiding in a star up there? If so, then how are we supposed to find her?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Ho'olheyak, you went into the library two months ago.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: I'm a historian, isn't it basically my job to visit libraries?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: We're talking about Maylander's 'library' here.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I don't recall authorizing that.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: You know I can't contain my curiosity.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Just like right now...

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: If I could trouble my employer with... a question that I've been awfully curious about...

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Your smoke.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Other than the clouds you puff out, the few wisps that slip into your body... where exactly do they go?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Is this why... you have the tip of your tail on my chest?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: I smell my favorite scent on you... history.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: So if it's at all possible, I'd love to get a good look at every little piece of your body for my research... Where should I start? Your head? Chest? Extremities?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: ...Ho'olheyak.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Do you really think... betraying the Maylander Foundation is the right choice here?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Of course... not.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Maylander holds most of this country's secrets. And in Columbia, secrets can be traded for wealth... or used as murder weapons.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: I spent three whole years before I finally managed to get into the Historical Society, and spent another three to gain your trust.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Do you know what six years means to me? Being a Maylander agent has already taken... one-seventh of my life.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Then you shouldn't be wasting the rest of it behind bars or on the run.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Yes, yes... I know.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: And yet... if my time here isn't enough to embrace what I've been yearning for my whole life, then what difference does it make if I live another ten years or one more minute?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Maylander won't allow anyone, least of all a defected agent, to access information they shouldn't be accessing.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: A shame you only have me to see in your last moments.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Then I can only pray to the stars... that the dead won't speak so easily.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Fine, let me switch up the question—

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: —Do you really think you can kill me?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: I'll never know... until I try.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Hrgh— Huh?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Your air manipulation shouldn't be affecting me... no, this isn't a K'uk'ulkan ability at all.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: You know me just so well, don't you.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: But, fortunately, I'm not exactly completely clueless as to what you are. Ordinary Arts have no effect on you, but...

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: ...A curse.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: The power of the oldest Sarkaz witchcraft, a soul-imprisoning curse.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: It's been an awfully long time since you've had a taste of something like this, hmm?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: That one year when a Maylander agent went deep into the Bleached Wasteland to investigate the ruins of the Sarkaz Royal Court, and suffered an unprecedented, life-threatening injury—

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I didn't expect Maylander to leave those files intact.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: You can't have thought that I ventured into Maylander's top secret database just for Kristen?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I did remind him that documenting everything isn't necessarily a good habit to have, all the time.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Hmph... According to you, only the long-lived would have such an extensive memory, while the rest of us just want to grab as much knowledge as we can, so naturally come up with different methods.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Otherwise, how could we short-lived beings hope to resist the control of people like you?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Huff... hah...

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: If you really want to destroy this body, you probably need a little more time.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: I have two minutes to spare.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: So, you're not even going to come out of hiding to greet me...

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: ...Banshee?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Weren't you just talking about how unwilling you are to show yourself?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Like I said, I have no interest in watching you murder your own boss.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: But he's more than just that.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Oh? Old acquaintances, are you?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Personally? Not at all.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: But my blood knows him.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Fascinating. I've been over it many times, and this guy here... doesn't smell Sarkaz.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Be careful of any tricks he might play. I don't want him to resurrect right after all the trouble I've gone through to kill him.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I won't let him interfere with the next step of the plan.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Hmm... I can't do it.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: A delicate trap you've laid. I had guessed that Ho'olheyak might have planted something in the sky, but I didn't expect a banshee's curse to be hidden in the noise of the construction site.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: My blood has taught me the power of words, and the sound of machinery clashing and colliding is the language I hear most.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: An amazing talent to have fooled even me. There are only a few banshees, including those in the Royal Court, who could make me suffer like this.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Were you born in Kazdel, or the Valley of the Banshees?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: It doesn't matter. My blood is not pure enough, and I haven't experienced any grand events either.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Right now, I'm just a engineer living in Columbia doing whatever I want.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: *cough*...haha... have you found a home... in Columbia?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Ah... so many years have passed by in a flash.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I've heard, that over the past two centuries, those two youths... Theresis and Theresa have finally built Kazdel as a Nomadic city.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I don't even know myself what Kazdel looks like today.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Are the streets still as crowded, the flags hanging on the city walls unchanged for a millennium, the undying furnace in the core still as hot as ever?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Can you relight my cigarette, child?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: This little spark can't hold the remaining warmth of your soul.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I know. I only... want to stay a little longer to ask you a few more questions.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: What did you see, in Kristen's dreams?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: ...The future.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Has she actually promised you... a change to the Sarkaz's fate? Do you believe she can do what no one has been able to accomplish over the past millennium?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: No, she only showed me a possibility.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: A possibility... that came from within myself.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Alright, Engineer Girl, if I could just trouble you to ask my darling employer if he has any last words?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: The fire is almost out.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Time moves too fast for an old man like me.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: The last question is mine.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: An ancient one like you must have seen the fall of many Kazdels, and surely you must have thought of and searched for a place—

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: (Speaks in Sarkaz) Where is the Sarkaz promised land?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Promised... land, hm...

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Time's up.
A silvery green tail shatters the Tin Man's sigh with a strong burst of wind.
The last spark fizzles out at the same time the cigarette hits the ground.
A bone whistle sounds.
Trimounts has never heard such a sound. Neither the residents in their deep sleep or the office workers working overtime will be aware of what has just happened.
Other than those who've made an appointment.

options: Rosmontis, did you hear that?

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Huh?

options: Logos was too busy to come to Trimounts, right?

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: My terminal says Logos has a lot to do. He hasn't trained with me for a long time, so I haven't been using my full strength in my sessions.

options: Don't make things hard for Mechanist.
It's been hard for Blaze and Sharp.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: My devices are like the Rhodes Island cabins, if they break down, it takes a long time for Mechanist and Closure to fix them.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Blaze and Sharp always complain that training with me is more tiring than going out on missions.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Before we left the landship, Raidian told me that Logos would come back with Amiya soon.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: I miss Amiya too. I miss her so much.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Doctor, will we be able to see them, after we finish this, and return to Rhodes Island?

options: I miss them too.
I hope we can see them soon too.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Doctor, did you make it there?

options: Yes, the message says we're meeting in this alley.
I think the Tin Man should be already waiting for me?
We'll go home soon, I promise.

steps.text: The alley is dark and silent, like an abyss.
Something rolls out from the murky shadows.
Perhaps it's due to its material hardness, but as it rubs against the ground, it eerily resembles a cog out of its wheel, a frightful rattle echoing through the darkness of the night.
It rolls straight to the alley entrance, where light and darkness meet.
It turns out to be a metal head.

The upper half is usually obscured by a hat's brim, and the mouth on its lower half often has a cigarette exhaling rings of smoke while spouting words that are at times perceptive, and other times incongruous.
But now there is no cigarette, no hat, no trench coat, or even the part that should be present past the neck.
There is only a head.

options: The Tin Man...
...is dead?

steps.text: I would take it easy, if I were you.
After all, if you do make any moves, I can't guarantee that your head won't end up rolling along with my old employer's there.

spans.text: make any moves, I can't guarantee that your head won't end up rolling along with my old employer's there.

options: Let's get to the point.
You didn't come here just to banter with me.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Two things—It's time for Rhodes Island to end your excursion in Trimounts, and the other, as you've just seen, the leader of the Maylander agents, the 'Tin Man' has been murdered. We need a culprit.

options: And you've picked me.
Should I feel honored?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Your frailty certainly affects the credibility of the idea.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: But the mundanity and perfectly enigmatic vibes of Rhodes Island makes you an excellent target for Maylander investigations, even if just for a bit.

options: You want to buy Kristen some time.
You want to buy yourself some time.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: It won't do you any good to look for other secrets, okay?

options: It's not like I can run.
It never hurts to get a better understanding of each other.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Are you going to try and call for help?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: You might want to lower your gaze, my tail won't exactly agree.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Or do you want to employ your expert negotiation techniques, to list a number of reasons why I can't do anything to you?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: What a pity that Trimounts is not Tkaronto, and your opponent is not some black-hearted pharma.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: I've had my eyes on you ever since you stepped into Trimounts.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: At first, none of this had anything to do with you... or Rhodes Island at all.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Even if you and Saria are moving in the same direction, roleplaying as heroic firefighters, why haven't you dispatched a few more men like that good old mechanic to mop things up quick?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: If you're not going to talk, then why don't I... tear your chest open and take a look at the secrets hiding inside?
The silvery green Liberi approaches.
Her plumage scrapes the fabric of your hood, emanating a soft but piercing sound.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: At first, I thought you were the same as those other eccentric scientists, trying to find some sort of revelation about the future in Kristen's research.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: After all, we're such a silly species, aren't we? Limited lifespan and unlimited ambition.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: The moment we realize the limits of what we can accomplish in our short lives, we become willing to surrender our arrogance for just a moment, and beg for a shortcut.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: But on you...*sniff*...I smell no trace of that desire.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: What do you dream of, and what of your past?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: I'm becoming very interested in you now, 'Doctor.'

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: But unfortunately, my colleagues are about to show.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Hold your friend's head in your hands, and enjoy a captivating session with Columbia's top agents. You might find yourself astonished.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Think through some answers to my questions during your interrogation.

options: I hope I don't give you the chance to run.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Wait...

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Why... are you here?

steps.name: Muelsyse?
steps.text: Heehee... did this hood ever come with a guarantee of who would be under it?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: ...A water clone.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Grrr. Any more tricks up your sleeve, pathetic Elf?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Doesn't matter. Dr. {@nickname} of Rhodes Island... we will see each other very soon.

spans.text: Doesn't matter. Dr. {@nickname} of Rhodes Island... we

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Doctor, there are a lot of people rushing towards that alley.

options: They're Maylander agents.
Rhodes Island has been set up.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It's a good thing you used your brains and 'borrowed' my clone for that meeting, otherwise you'd have fallen into that horrible woman's trap for real.

options: She's definitely left evidence implicating Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You heard everything she said over the comms, right? Did we make enemies of both Maylander and the military?

options: I'm afraid so.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Ah... hahaha... you're not joking, are you?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Doctor, if you and the Tin Man had any plans, now would a good time to share them, you know?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Your silence implies... Wait, Doctor, you can't mean that he...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Something really happened to that mega mysterious super agent in the trench coat with a tin can for a head?!

options: I heard a banshee's bone whistle.
The knell has tolled for him.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: That was a bone whistle?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Wait, banshee, you say? Of the Sarkaz variety?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Was it for Kristen? Did she...?
Muelsyse suddenly falls silent. She looks up at the sky above Trimounts.
There is nothing up there besides thousands of stars.
You cannot help but recall Ho'olheyak's question from earlier.
Why did you come to Trimounts?

options: Kristen... What sort of person is she exactly?
What exactly is the dream that she's chasing?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Quick, Silence! Over here!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Mmm...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: This alarm... did something happen to Director Jara...?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Silence, are you okay?!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'm fine. Saria...

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: I'll help you carry her.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Your face is all sweaty, if Saria doesn't wake up now, they're gonna catch us!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Don't push the blame onto Saria.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: But your face... you look like you're about to...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'm fine, Ifrit. I just happened to remember what happened earlier.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I watched her fall in front of me, and my very first reaction was not worry, or surprise, but regret.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Because... you were mad at her?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Yes. If that really was the last conversation we ever had, I didn't want to think... that I was blaming her.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Actually I've never... I just...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I don't know who else can hear me out.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Then just patch things up.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: And then, when Saria wakes up, we can go back together. How about it?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: She'll return here the moment she wakes up.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: That's the sort of woman she is.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Fine, I think I get it, neither of you is gonna go home, are you?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Then, why not work together?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Work together...?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Yeah, Silence. Even though you got some new gear on, you're still a doctor. If you keep on running like this, you're gonna get hurt or even die.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: I know Saria is a great fighter. Even I've started to know that teamwork's important, yet she still likes to work alone.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: If it weren't for us, Saria would be in an even worse situation right now!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Neither of you wanted me to tag along, but at the very least, you gotta promise me that you'll work with Saria.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Otherwise, the two of you will worry about me, and I'll worry about you guys too!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...Ifrit.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Just say yes or no. I'll even behave and go back to the Doctor. Just promise me!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Some words are easier to say when you're a team, right?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Where did you learn all this?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: The Doctor passed taught me all these people skills!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...I'll think about it.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Great!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Uh, Silence, what's that over there?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: A Transmitter... that just appeared?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: It's all silvery and flowy. Real pretty!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Don't touch it!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Ifrit, that's... very dangerous.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Dangerous? No way, more than my flames?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It's another product of Rhine's experiments.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: For real? Then I'll burn it up!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: No, just wait and see. Don't be too quick to destroy it.
A small lump of silvery substance gushes inside the test tube.
Ever since it left Parvis's home, it has lingered without a target direction, as if it has lost its hub directive.
As if its only mission is to lead her to Parvis.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Profess... Parvis never does anything without purpose.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: His appearance earlier, couldn't have just been him wanting to chat with me... he deliberately led me to think he was the goal in this race for the Transmitter.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Could it be... the truth was never...

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Silence, the door's over here!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Agh—!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: How could... did someone spot us?
Stand back, Ifrit.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Calcification...!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Saria, you're awake! Hooray!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But you're...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I'm fine.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You're not bluffing a doctor that easily.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I'm just holding this door until it's safe enough for you to leave. QED, I'm perfectly fine.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: The military mechs are closing in on our position.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: This path is no longer safe.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Director Jara...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: She wouldn't hand over the information that easily.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: And so, there is only one possibility remaining.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: ...Ten minutes.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: They should have run into Blake's people by now.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: The old Saria would have probably stood a chance to escape unscathed.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: However, she's injured and carrying two extra burdens. Want to guess how long she can last in front of a fully armed special forces unit?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Your phone is ringing, ma'am.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: It's me.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Of course. I'm always willing... to serve Columbia.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Thank you for the advice.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: By now, you should be willing to believe me that I did try my best.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I tried my hardest just to secure this opportunity to talk. If you had agreed with me earlier, then our Defense Director's life would at the very least not be in danger.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: But you still sent them on that path... to that secret passage known only to Maylander agents.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Saria might die because of you, and the next one to go may well be the one you're most concerned about.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I'm hoping from the bottom of my heart that you think the question over.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Where the hell is Kristen Wright?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Director Jara... works for Maylander?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I investigated her ten years ago and found nothing. It was only when the Tin Man showed up and I left Rhine Lab that I got more clues to confirm it.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: She's been at Rhine for a long time.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: She knew Kristen even before I did.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Ifrit, attack the window on your left.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Gotcha!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: It's so sturdy!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: The glass in the experimental labs is all reinforced, so ordinary impacts aren't going to be able to smash them.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: And if we break them now, we'll attract the attention of the soldiers downstairs.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: We can use my fire to cut through the glass.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: I can control my flames already, so I'll be able to do it.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: (The teacher mentioned this in my Originium Arts classes... fire can be tempered, be silent, and become a quiet anger.)

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: (Make my flames into a sword.)

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: (Make my flames into a single thread——)

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Hyah!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: It cracked... a little bit!

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: *cough*...*cough*...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You've split the enamel.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Saria, just hold on a little longer!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: I'm halfway through, I can do it!

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Focus, Ifrit. Don't get distracted.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: When you were unconscious, Director Jara told me that there's no way you can fight against the entire country.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: So if it is as you say, that Maylander and the military have come to some kind of agreement, then we truly are facing off the entire country right now.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Your heart rate and body temperature are spiking near their limits, and you've only just woken up. Your body is taking a serious toll.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Perhaps.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Saria, you're at your limit.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Silence, Jara modified your drone. I've seen... the prototype blueprints.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: When did you...?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Its current load-bearing capacity is at least two adults for a short distance glide.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Get out through the hole Ifrit opened, and the drone will be able to take you to the roof of the opposite building.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You'll have to act fast.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I'll wait for you to go over, and then I'll exit through this door and divert the pursuers. Their numbers are many, and I won't be able to fend them off for long.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...Saria.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You still haven't given me an answer.

a.text: Your inability to make a genuine stand against Rhine, is it because deep in your bones, you've always been the same as them...? The same as Control?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Sorry, Silence.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I thought it through, and I'm unable to give you a definite answer.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: If Kristen's experiment violates any laws that shouldn't have been broken, I will stop her. Just like all the wrongs Rhine has committed over the years—the wrong should be made right.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: For I've always believed that the stronger one is, the less rash they should be acting.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: But if I were to return to the past, back to when Kristen and I first met, when everything had yet to happen...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I would not have stopped the Kristen then. I would not have stopped the birth of Rhine Lab.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Yes, even if I knew that Rhine would create so much suffering in the future, even if I could foresee the ambitions of Kristen, Parvis and Ferdinand growing out of control...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I would still stand with them.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Saria... your answer might be even more definitive than you think.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Silence, Saria! Did you guys see that? I opened it!

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Go, Silence.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: If there's anything else you would like to know, we can wait until this is all over. And I'll tell you.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Silence? Silence?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Why are you spacing out? We gotta get moving.

a.text: 'Poor Liberi. None of this has anything to do with you.'
'What exactly is it that you want? Truth, justice, or peace?'
'I will tell you what you want to know.'
'And yet, even if you know it all, what can you do?'

steps.text: This is not the answer I want.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: A drone's... belt?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Silence, what are you doing?!
The whirring of a drone starting up comes from behind.
The unreinforced door at the end of the corridor is about to melt under the impact of the energy weapon.
Saria is suspended in midair, holding Ifrit in one arm, stretching the other out towards Silence, trying to grab her.
But Silence doesn't return her grip, and retraces the path she's taken in reverse.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I should have talked with you sooner, Saria.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I only just came to understand why I can't help but get mad at you.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I thought it was from the falling out we had during the 'Diαbolic Crisis.'

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Or that I'm dissatisfied with the way you insist on shouldering everything yourself.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But actually... the one I'm most annoyed with is myself.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: The blame I push onto you for not doing enough, it's only because... I built a habit of depending on you.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I had hoped you could change Control, just like I once hoped the Professor could save Ifrit, and that Control could change Rhine Lab... I had hoped every deadlock would be solved by someone stronger.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'm so weak, aren't I?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: On the one hand, I loathe the powerful figures that manipulate everything and treat innocent lives like expendable resources and numbers.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: On the other hand, I still pin my hopes for the future on people stronger in not just power, but also morality and empathy.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Only now do I understand that no one can truly carry everything on their own, that it's beyond the capacity of a single individual.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Everyone who has been willing to help me on the way here, Rhodes Island, Director Muelsyse, Director Jara, and you...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: All of you want me to stay out of it.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: If you hadn't collapsed in front of me, if Ifrit hadn't been in danger, I might have just obediently thrown in the towel.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But now—I won't back down.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I refuse to allow myself to stay under your wings. I refuse to accept that I can only stand in vain as the gunfire rings right above us and open my arms to the injured.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: This time, I will step into the flames before any of you.
The drone sends the two to a lower floor of the neighboring building. Saria smashes a window and they land smoothly.
There must be more of Ferdinand's people on the lookout downstairs, but as long as there's room for action, she believes she can find a way to break through the encirclement.
However...

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Silence... what are you doing?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Silence, hurry up and fly over here with your drone!
Ifrit anxiously yells at the room across, but Silence takes a long look at them before turning her back.
Just as Silence begins to turn, Saria gets a look at her eyes.
They are brimming with regret.
But more than that, is determination.

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Ferdinand, we've got someone in the corridor.

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: She says she has business with you.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: ...Silence?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Why are you...?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'm sorry, Director Jara. I've already made up my mind. I have unfinished business, so I can't leave just yet.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I remember you, Parvis's stellar student. You and Elena gave me such a headache back at Site 359.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Yes, my name is Silence.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I would like to make a deal with you.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: A deal? Do you really think I would let Saria go?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: This isn't up to you.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: No, this is the only thing that's up to me.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: That's... Transmitter, from Site 359.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: What are you doing?! Even if you put the Transmitter into your body, it's not going to work, Dorothy's 'hub' was destroyed!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: The new 'hub' is in Kristen's hands.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: That's impossible. That was my experiment, mine and Dorothy's...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: A short while ago, I met Dr. Parvis. His laboratory was storing a large amount of Transmitter.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Director Clooney, you must have realized it long ago. You just don't want to admit it... You would rather believe your failure was owed to a bad move, than to believe that Control was playing you the whole time.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Did you really never consider the possibility?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: She's the one that's working more closely with the military, she had countless ways to kill your experiment with Dorothy in its infancy—

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: —But then why did she only show up after your experiment succeeded?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: We still have a chance.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Whatever Kristen is trying to do with Transmitter, she hasn't succeeded yet.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Director Clooney, bring me to her.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: The Transmitter is inside me. I'll become your beacon to locate Kristen.
